summary: Iteration 5: Phase 3 Order Tracking & Delivery features tested end-to-end. Backend (20/20 tests pass): admin orders dashboard, status updates, cancel, delivery agent promote/assign, notifications, customer tracking, order ownership enforcement. Frontend: Admin Orders Dashboard, Delivery Dashboard, Order Tracking timeline, Notification bell+dropdown all render and work correctly. Found 1 HIGH frontend bug (MyOrdersPage premature redirect) and 1 backend code-quality bug (KeyError on expires_at).

minor.issue: Uses session["expires_at"] which raises KeyError -> 500 if any user_sessions doc lacks expires_at. Should use session.get("expires_at") with None-check and treat missing as expired or non-blocking. Discovered when seeded delivery_agent session without expires_at returned 500.

ui_bugs.issue: Customer route /my-orders redirects to /businesses. Root cause: useEffect at line 26 checks `if (!isAuthenticated) navigate('/login')` WITHOUT waiting for AuthContext `loading` to be false. On mount, isAuthenticated is initially false (auth still loading) -> navigates to /login -> Login.jsx useEffect then sees auth loaded with role='customer' -> redirects to /businesses. The page never renders, so Track-Order links on My Orders are inaccessible.
ui_bugs.fix_suggestion: Use `const { isAuthenticated, loading } = useAuth();` and guard: `if (loading) return; if (!isAuthenticated) { navigate('/login'); return; }` Also gate the loading spinner JSX on loading state. Same pattern should be audited across OrderTrackingPage and any other page that reads isAuthenticated synchronously.

action_items: FIX (HIGH): MyOrdersPage.jsx must wait for AuthContext loading=false before navigating to /login. Pattern: destructure { isAuthenticated, loading } and `if (loading) return;` before the auth check. Audit OrderTrackingPage and other pages for the same pattern.
FIX (MEDIUM): server.py get_current_user should use session.get('expires_at') with safe handling to avoid 500 on malformed sessions.
Consider adding a global loading gate inside AuthProvider so children only mount once auth is resolved - prevents this class of bug app-wide.
critical_code_review_comments: AuthContext exposes `loading` but most pages do not consume it -> race condition between AuthContext.checkAuth() and useEffect redirects in protected pages.
server.py session expiry check throws KeyError instead of treating missing field as expired - should be defensive.
/delivery and other role-protected pages rely on ProtectedRoute. Verified ProtectedRoute correctly routes delivery_agent to /delivery and blocks customers.

Delivery dashboard 'Not Delivered' button is shown even for orders in 'confirmed' state (before admin marks 'preparing'). Confirm intended UX - delivery agent should arguably not be able to mark not_delivered until they actually attempt delivery.
order_management_routes.py uses .find(...).to_list(length=None) - acceptable for current data volume but consider pagination as orders grow.

rca of the issue: MyOrdersPage redirect bug RCA: 1) User navigates to /my-orders 2) AuthProvider mounts with loading=true, isAuthenticated=false, user=null 3) MyOrdersPage useEffect runs immediately, sees !isAuthenticated -> navigate('/login') 4) Login.jsx mounts; meanwhile AuthContext.checkAuth() completes -> isAuthenticated=true, user.role='customer' 5) Login.jsx useEffect on [isAuthenticated, user] fires -> navigate('/businesses'). Reproduction: visit /my-orders with valid customer session cookie. Mitigation: gate the auth check on loading=false (see action_items).
